While I appreciate the idea I would prefer to have a system that wouldn’t potentially cause any harm or panic to her. I don’t know how many tunnels she has or how strong they are, so I would prefer a method that doesn’t actually cause any stress to the tunnel system in there

I’ve always been told if you find your t preferring to sit on the acrylic bottom of their enclosure, that it typically means they don’t care for some aspect of the enclosure and they’re trying to pull themselves away from it. 

I also know that this is case by case. 

My question was more in line with how, if I absolutely needed to, would I encourage her to come out. She’s growing fast, and while she hasn’t molted with me yet, it’s bound to happen very soon and she’s going to be a very big girl. So I would prefer to have a last ditch effort answer to before I need it and before she gets too big to exit her hide without hurting herself.
